bands.1:
You have won Madame Pause's badge. Now she is on your side.

"Maxx's lodge has a Comment Control Room, full stop," she says. "It deletes every question, full stop."

Stoppit, her red robin, fluffs up on her ski pole.

Indi has made a disguise. It is one giant snowman. The whole crew hides inside it, with Madame Pause.

"It has sixteen legs," says Tully.

"Snowmen come in all shapes," says Indi.

Gus holds up a jar. Inside is one grey sock. "The Stink Sock! I wore it for five weeks. That's not gross. That's science."

Two Goldies guard the lodge door. The snowman shuffles past. Gus opens the jar. The Goldies turn green and run away.

Zed types GORGEOUSME into the keypad. The door opens.

Inside, a big screen shows Maxx's stream. Rows of little gold robots sit in front of it. A sign says, "DELETE ANY COMMENT WITH A QUESTION MARK."

"Is it scared?" Tap. Gone. "Is that a cage?" Tap. Gone.

Cages fill the corner. There are Dotumbles, Stashlets and a jar of Throngle moths.

A gold drive hums by the bots. The label says, "DELETED QUESTIONS: 4,812,337."

"Proof," you whisper. You put it in your bag.

Then a Goldie bursts in. "Stop them bots!" he yells.

The bots stop. Then they switch each other off!

"He forgot the comma, full stop," says Madame Pause. "He meant, 'Stop them, comma, bots.' Instead, he told the bots to stop the bots, full stop."

Wren opens every cage. The Dotumbles roll out. The Throngles fly out in a cloud. The Goldie is covered in moths.

You all ride the chairlift down, laughing.

On the boat, Gus checks Maxx's stream. With no bots, questions are piling up. Then a new one pops up.

"Is that the Soggy Biscuit crew?"

You look up. A MaxxCam drone is right above the mast.

"Stay gold, Captain," says Maxx's voice. "You're live."
bands.2:
You have won Madame Pause's badge, so now the Keeper of Comma Cay is on your side.

"Maxx's lodge has a Comment Control Room, full stop," she says. "Every question anyone asks him, comma, it deletes, full stop."

Stoppit, her round red robin, fluffs up on her ski pole.

Indi has made the disguise of the Chapter. It is one enormous snowman costume, built from three bedsheets and a carrot. The whole crew is supposed to fit inside it, plus Madame Pause.

"Nobody looks twice at a snowman," says Indi. "It's a snowy island."

"It has sixteen legs," says Tully.

"Snowmen come in all shapes."

Gus holds up a sealed jar. Inside is one grey ski sock. "The Stink Sock," he says. "I've worn it for five weeks straight. That's not gross. That's science."

Two Goldies in gold tracksuits guard the lodge door. The snowman shuffles past them.

"Nice snowman," says a Goldie.

"Thanks," says the snowman, in eight voices.

Then Gus opens the jar. Both Goldies turn green and sprint down the mountain.

Zed types MAXXISGREAT into the keypad. Wrong. He tries GORGEOUSME, and the door slides open. "From terrible to tragic," he says.

Inside, a giant screen shows Maxx's live stream. In front of it sit rows of gold robots the size of toasters, each with one long finger. A sign says, "RULE ONE: DELETE ANY COMMENT WITH A QUESTION MARK."

"Is it scared?" Tap. Gone. "Is that a cage?" Tap. Gone.

Glass cages fill one corner. Dotumbles curl up inside, and a cloud of Throngle moths flutters in a jar.

Beside the bots, a gold drive hums. Its label says, "DELETED QUESTIONS. DO NOT LOOK. 4,812,337 AND COUNTING."

"Proof," you whisper, and slip it into your bag.

Suddenly, a Goldie bursts back in. "Stop them bots!" he yells.

Every bot freezes. Then they reach out their long fingers and switch each other off.

"He forgot the comma, full stop," says Madame Pause happily. "He meant, 'Stop them, comma, bots.' Instead, comma, he told the bots to stop the bots, full stop."

Wren flings open the cages. Dotumbles roll out like marbles. The Throngles burst out in a cloud, and the Goldie vanishes under a blizzard of moths.

You all creak down the mountain on the chairlift, laughing.

Back on the boat, Gus checks Maxx's stream. With no bots left, the questions are piling up. Then a new one appears at the top.

"Is that the Soggy Biscuit crew on the chairlift?"

Slowly, you look up. A MaxxCam drone is hovering above the mast, its red light blinking.

"Stay gold, Captain," says Maxx's voice. "You're live."
bands.3:
You have won Madame Pause's badge, and with it, a ride on her private chairlift, an old wooden one that creaks like a haunted rocking chair.

"The gold lodge has one door, comma, two guards and no sense of humour, full stop," she says. "Inside is the Comment Control Room, full stop. Every question anyone asks Maxx, comma, it deletes, full stop."

Stoppit, her round red robin, fluffs up on her ski pole as if to agree.

Indi has been up all night on disguises. When she unveils them, there is a long silence. She has built one enormous snowman costume out of three bedsheets, a mop bucket and a carrot. The whole crew is supposed to fit inside it, plus Madame Pause.

"Nobody will look twice at a snowman," Indi says. "It's a snowy island."

"It has sixteen legs," says Tully.

"Snowmen come in all shapes."

Gus has brought a sealed jar with a single grey ski sock inside. "The Stink Sock," he says proudly. "I've worn it every day for five weeks. That's not gross. That's science."

At the top of the chairlift, two Goldies in gold tracksuits guard the lodge. The snowman shuffles towards them. Its carrot falls off, and Mo sticks it back on upside down.

"Nice snowman," says one Goldie.

"Thanks," says the snowman, in eight voices.

Then Gus unscrews the jar. The smell rolls out like fog. Both Goldies turn green and sprint down the mountain with their hands over their noses.

The keypad on the inner door wants a password. Zed tries MAXXISGREAT. Wrong. He tries GORGEOUSME, and the door slides open. "He's levelled up," says Zed. "From terrible to tragic."

The Comment Control Room is the size of a basketball court. One wall is a giant screen showing Maxx's live stream, with comments pouring up the side like a waterfall. In front of it sit rows of Deletebots, gold robots the size of toasters, each with one long finger. Above them, a sign says, "RULE ONE: DELETE ANY COMMENT WITH A QUESTION MARK."

"Is it scared?" Tap. Gone. "Why is it shaking?" Tap. Gone.

In the corner, glass cages are stacked to the ceiling. Dotumbles are curled up asleep inside, Stashlets press their noses to the glass, and a cloud of Throngle moths flutters in a jar.

Behind the bots sits a gold drive, humming. Its label says, "DELETED QUESTIONS. DO NOT LOOK. 4,812,337 AND COUNTING."

"Proof," you whisper, and slide it into your bag.

At that moment, a Goldie bursts back in, his eyes still watering. He points at Wren and shouts, "Stop them bots!"

Every bot freezes. Then, one by one, they reach out their long fingers and switch each other off.

"He forgot the comma, full stop," says Madame Pause happily. "He meant, 'Stop them, comma, bots.' Instead, comma, he told the bots to stop the bots, full stop. Tragic, full stop."

Wren flings open the cages. Dotumbles roll out like dropped marbles, and the Throngles pour out in a cloud that fills the room. The Goldie disappears under a blizzard of moths.

You all pile onto the old chairlift with the Creatures in your arms and creak back down the mountain, laughing.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, Gus opens Maxx's stream on the cracked tablet. With no bots left, the questions are piling up. Then a brand-new one appears at the top, posted three seconds ago.

"Is that the Soggy Biscuit crew on the chairlift?"

Slowly, you look up. A MaxxCam drone is hovering above the mast, its red light blinking.

"Stay gold, Captain," says Maxx's voice from the drone. "You're live."
bands.4:
You have won Madame Pause's badge, and with it, a ride on her private chairlift, an old wooden one that creaks like a haunted rocking chair.

"The gold lodge has one door, comma, two guards and no sense of humour, full stop," she says, as Stoppit fluffs up on her pole. "But it also has a Comment Control Room, full stop. Every question anyone asks Maxx, comma, it deletes, full stop."

Indi has spent all night on disguises. When she unveils them, there is a long, painful silence. She has built one enormous snowman costume out of three bedsheets, a mop bucket and a carrot. The whole crew is supposed to fit inside it, plus Madame Pause, with the smallest people on top.

"Nobody will look twice at a snowman," Indi says confidently. "It's a snowy island."

"It has sixteen legs," says Tully.

"Snowmen come in all shapes."

Gus has brought his gadget of the Chapter: a single grey ski sock in a sealed jar. "The Stink Sock," he says proudly. "I've worn it every day for five weeks, through two footy matches and a swamp. That's not gross. That's science."

At the top of the chairlift, two Goldies in gold tracksuits and gold earmuffs guard the lodge door. The snowman shuffles towards them. Its carrot falls off. Mo picks it up and sticks it back on, upside down.

"Reef Rays are losing by thirty," whispers Tully, from somewhere near the snowman's knees.

"Not now," hisses everyone.

"Nice snowman," says one Goldie.

"Thanks," says the snowman, in eight voices.

The Goldies shrug and let it waddle past. Behind them, Gus unscrews the jar. The smell rolls out like a fog bank. Both Goldies turn green, then grey, then sprint down the mountain with their hands clamped over their noses.

Inside, the lodge is warm and gold and humming. The keypad on the inner door asks for a password, and Zed starts muttering. "Okay so he's used MAXXISGREAT before and he's used ILOVEME and he probably thinks those are clever so maybe he's added..."

Stoppit pecks him on the ear.

"Sorry," says Zed. He types GORGEOUSME, and the door slides open. "He's levelled up his passwords. From terrible to tragic."

The Comment Control Room is the size of a basketball court. One whole wall is a screen showing Maxx's live stream, with comments pouring up the side like a waterfall. In front of it sit rows and rows of Deletebots: gold robots the size of toasters, each with a single long finger. Above them, a sign says, "RULE ONE: DELETE ANY COMMENT WITH A QUESTION MARK."

You watch the comments flood in. "Is it scared?" Tap. Gone. "Why is it shaking?" Tap. Gone. "Is that a cage?" Tap. Gone. The bots never stop.

In the corner, glass cages are stacked to the ceiling. Dotumbles are curled up asleep inside, Stashlets press their noses to the glass, and a whole cloud of Throngles flutters inside a jar.

Behind the bots sits a gold hard drive, humming hotter than everything else. Its label says, "DELETED QUESTIONS. DO NOT LOOK. 4,812,337 AND COUNTING."

"Proof," you whisper, and slide it into your bag.

At exactly that moment, a Goldie bursts back through the door, his eyes still streaming. He points at Wren and bellows at the bots, "Stop them bots!"

Every bot freezes. Then, one by one, they reach out their long fingers and switch each other off.

"He forgot the comma, full stop," says Madame Pause happily. "He meant, 'Stop them, comma, bots.' Instead, comma, he told the bots to stop the bots, full stop. Tragic, full stop."

Wren flings open the cages. Dotumbles roll out like dropped marbles, Stashlets scurry for the door, and the Throngles pour out in a fluttering cloud that fills the room. The Goldie disappears under a blizzard of moths.

You all pile onto the creaking chairlift with the Creatures in your arms and sway back down the mountain, laughing so hard that the whole chair wobbles.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, Gus opens Maxx's stream on the cracked tablet. With no bots left, the questions are piling up, thousands of them, from all over the world. Then a brand-new one appears at the top, posted three seconds ago.

"Is that the Soggy Biscuit crew on the chairlift?"

Everyone goes very still. Slowly, you look up. Hovering above the mast, its red light blinking, is a MaxxCam drone.

It has been filming the whole time.

"Stay gold, Captain," says Maxx's voice from the drone. "You're live."
